newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: FOCUS-DEALERS MIXED ON HERMIS RESULTS, GAINS SEEN.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-DEALERS MIXED ON HERMIS RESULTS, GAINS SEEN.

text.p: Lithuanian dealers were generally bullish on Hermis Bank shares but divided in their reaction to its first-half results.
The bank said on Wednesday that its first half net profit was 14.3 million litas after posting a profit of 27.4 million litas for all of 1996.
The bank's chairwoman, Nadiezhda Novickiene, told Reuters the bank was pleased with its first half result and saw no need to revise its 1997 forecast of a profit of 40.6 million litas.

Novickiene pointed to the impressive growth of the bank's assets, which have risen 39 percent this year to 741.6 million litas, as a good sign which bodes well for the bank's profitability in the second half of the year.
The bank's shares rose to 198.20 litas from 195.00 litas on Wednesday ahead of the result announcement.

"The market was expecting higher profit figures from Hermis Bank for the first half of the year but they were high enough to push the price further," Arvydas Jacikevichius, a broker with Suprema brokerage house, told Reuters.
Saules Merkys, a broker with Vilfima, was more upbeat.
"I think that the present results of Hermis are really good and I see no reasons why the bank will not reach its forecast for the year," Merkys told Reuters.
"Hermis is one of the most active shares on the bourse and there is growing investor interest in Hermis the bank," he said.
He added that the bank has been undervalued for some time and forecast that its price will reach 200 litas in the short-term and stay around that level.
"Hermis Bank's shares are still comparatively cheap, it is a good bank and has room to grow," said Kestutis Kvainauskas, a dealer with Vilniaus Bank's brokerage department.
He added that Lithuania's share market was still underdeveloped and did not always respond to corporate and banking results, good or bad.
